newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-AUXERRE WIN AS TOP TEAMS DRAW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AUXERRE WIN AS TOP TEAMS DRAW.

text.p: Auxerre sounded a warning to Ajax Amnsterdam ahead of their European Cup Champions' League clash next week with a 2-0 home win that lifted them nearer the French first division leaders on Friday.

Pacesetters Paris Saint Germain retained their unbeaten record in a 0-0 draw at home against Monaco in the clash of the title favourites, a highly technical but ultimately sterile match at Parc des Princes. PSG have kept six clean sheets in six games so far.
The Parisians retained their one-point lead over Lens, also held to a scoreless draw at home by Cannes. Monaco are third, two points further back in a group of five teams on 11 points.

Champions Auxerre, surprise losers at Strasbourg on Tuesday, scored through Algerian midfielder Moussa Saib and striker Lilian Laslandes in the opening 20 minutes to climb to fourth behind Monaco on goal difference.

The closest Paris Saint Germain came to scoring was when France striker Patrice Loko hit the post early in the second half after Panama's Julio Cesar Dely Valdes had come off the bench to give their attack more penetration.
Monaco, the division's highest scorers, looked sharper in front of goal in a fast-paced opening 45 minutes with Brazilian Anderson shooting just over the crossbar.
Nantes, champions in 1995, continued their worst start to a first division season since promotion in 1963 with a 3-1 defeat at Le Havre.
A penalty proved the turning point, defender Teddy Bertin putting the north coast side ahead from the spot in the 51st minute after handball by midfielder Jocelyn Gourvennec.
Defender Laurent Guyot put Nantes ahead in the 33rd minute from a cross from the right, but striker Stephane Samson equalised with a low shot on the stroke of halftime.
Croat Ardian Kozniku made the match safe for Le Havre with their third goal from a rebound off the woodwork in the 66th minute.

Yugoslav Miladin Becanovic took sole lead in the scorers table when he equalised for sixth-placed Lille with a penalty in the 64th minute, his fifth goal of the season, in the 1-1 home draw against Guingamp.
Liberian Christopher Wreh, formerly of Monaco, put Guingamp ahead in the 58th minute.
Metz are in fifth place after their 1-0 home win over bottom team Nancy. Senegal's Amara Traore scored from a corner in the 62nd minute.
